one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban argues that with the COVID-19 emergency at full pitch, Congress, the Palace, and the PSA Board must fast-track implementation of RA 11055 (the Philippine Identification System Act of 2018, the 'PhilID') to deliver the Bayanihan to Heal as One cash subsidy of P5,000-P8,000 a month for two months to 18 million low-income households and to enable rapid COVID-19 contact tracing. He defends the law's constitutionality by surveying jurisprudence: Ople v. Torres (July 23, 1998) struck down FVR's AO 308 only because executive issuances cannot establish a national ID -- Justice Puno's privacy-based argument did not command a majority -- and Kilusang Mayo Uno v. Director General (April 19, 2006, 11-2) upheld EO 420, articulating the three-prong test under which legislation is required (appropriation; universal compulsion across branches and citizens; data going beyond what is routinely required). Because the PhilID's data fields -- PSN, name, sex, blood type, optional marital status, place of birth, photo, date of birth, address, plus a QR code with limited fingerprint information -- are already publicly disclosed on driver's licenses, passports, senior IDs, SSS, and GSIS cards, RA 11055 will, 'in my humble opinion,' easily survive challenge, and the leftists Duterte blamed on national TV-radio will fail in their opposition. He notes that Sotto and Lacson have signaled a Senate inquiry into the implementation delay despite over P6 billion in GAA allotments over three years, and points to the recent replacement of NEDA Secretary Pernia by Finance Usec Karl Chua as the new PSA Board chair. He closes with a directive 'Verily, I urge the PSA Board... to act pronto lest an enraged President Duterte tongue-lashes it again.'
